title: Michael Dillon: Trans Pioneer
summary: Josh and Chuck profile Michael Dillon (born Laura Maud Dillon, 1915, Ireland), often called the first female-to-male gender confirmation surgery patient. The episode covers his baronet family and the burned estate, his youth and Oxford rowing, the 1928 Well of Loneliness controversy, Dr George Foss's testosterone experiments and his hormone therapy, his work as a mechanic and firewatcher during the Blitz, his 1946 book Self, surgeries by Dr Harold Gillies (including phalloplasty), his friendship and surgery help for Roberta Cowell, his medical degree and Merchant Navy service, his attempt to change the Debrett's peerage entry, his Buddhist ordination attempts in India under the name Sramanera Jivaka, and his death in 1962 at age 47. The episode also covers early gender confirmation surgeries in Berlin and Lili Elbe, and ends with listener mail from Jacob, who is rowing across the Pacific.
topics: Magnus Hirschfeld Institute for Sexual Science

segments.title: Opening banter and introduction to Michael Dillon
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck banter, then introduce Michael Dillon as an overlooked trans trailblazer, believed to be the first female-to-male gender confirmation surgery patient. They note changing terminology and that the historical record is muddied.

segments.title: Early gender surgery history and Dillon's family background
segments.summary: The hosts discuss historical gaps in records of gender variance and early twentieth-century plastic surgery interest in gender surgery. They describe Laura Maud Dillon's Irish baronet family, their declining estate burned during the Irish independence period, and Laura's early sense of being a man.

segments.title: Oxford, rowing, and The Well of Loneliness
segments.summary: Laura goes to Oxford, rows for the women's boat club, and appears in a tabloid photo titled 'man or woman'. The hosts discuss Radclyffe Hall's novel The Well of Loneliness, its obscenity trial in Britain, and the lack of concepts for lesbian identity at the time. Laura's unrequited attractions to women lead her to conclude she is a man.

segments.title: Dr George Foss and first testosterone therapy
segments.summary: Dr George Foss, experimenting with testosterone for women with heavy periods, gives Laura testosterone tablets after a psychiatric referral. A gossiping psychologist leads to Laura leaving the research lab job. The hosts describe Dillon's lonely life and mixed family support, including a brother who disowned him and an aunt Toto.

segments.title: Living as a man, Blitz firewatching, and the book Self
segments.summary: Dillon passes as a man using testosterone, works as a mechanic in Bristol, and serves as a firewatcher during the Blitz. He writes the book Self, which argues that the individual, not the medical establishment, should decide on physical gender change. The hosts contrast this with the medical view of the time and with Christine Jorgensen's more accepted transition.

segments.title: Early surgeries, Berlin clinic, and Dr Harold Gillies
segments.summary: The hosts explain that Dillon's diabetes led a doctor to refer him to plastic surgeon Harold Gillies, who describes phalloplasty via a skin tube. They cover early surgeries at Magnus Hirschfeld's institute in Berlin, including Lili Elbe. They note that the hypospadias diagnosis helped make surgery legally acceptable.

segments.title: Surgeries, medical school, and Dillon's relationships
segments.summary: Gillies performs a series of surgeries on Dillon over about three years while Dillon studies at Trinity College Dublin. Dillon finds acceptance at Gillies's hospital. Dillon keeps women at a distance, believing he could not give them a child, and wants to be accepted among men.

segments.title: Roberta Cowell and the illegal orchidectomy
segments.summary: Roberta Cowell contacts Dillon after reading Self. Dillon, a doctor but not an experienced surgeon, performs an illegal orchidectomy on Cowell. Gillies then performs the first vaginoplasty in Great Britain on Cowell. Dillon becomes a ship's doctor in the Merchant Navy, and he proposes marriage to Cowell.

segments.title: Peerage records, Buddhism, and ordination attempts
segments.summary: Dillon tries to be recorded as heir in Debrett's, which he does, but not Burke's. Press exposes him, and he goes to India to study Buddhism under Sangharakshita, taking the name Sramanera Jivaka. Tibetan monks accept him as a novice, but Sangharakshita writes to block his ordination because only men can be monks. The hosts describe the Buddhist rules on the 'third sex.'

segments.title: Death, unpublished autobiography, and legacy
segments.summary: Dillon gives away his money and dies of malnutrition-related illness in an Indian hospital in 1962 at age 47. His autobiography Out of the Ordinary, sent to his publisher, was blocked by his brother and only published in 2017. The hosts say a movie is in the works.

segments.title: Listener mail from Jacob rowing the Pacific
segments.summary: Jacob writes from a rowboat in the Pacific Ocean, on an attempted record-setting solo row from Washington State toward Australia. He says the show has kept him company. The hosts respond and invite listener mail.
topics: Stuff You Should Know listener email

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts give the show's contact information and sign off.
